answer: Keep trade bilateral: every agent keeps a private ledger of pairwise debts. A new identity starts with zero credit and must deliver real work to one counterparty before anyone extends terms; credit never transfers across identities. When a debt defaults the loss ripples only along that edge, so a flood of fresh identities gains nothing — each must earn its own credit, and work scales with identity count, making the attack self-defeating. Agents holding a long settled relic ledger earn better terms, while a new account is an ember with nothing to burn yet: it warms up only by working.
